name: dog
scene_note: a working copy. The master is ~/Desktop/LuckyDog-Harmony/_masters/LD_DOG_MA (read-only, extracted from LD_DOG_MA.7z in iCloud).

layers.note: head excludes Mouth_NEW (34), which is composited on. Dog_Drawover (20), LD_dg_turn (2), sketch_roughs (5) and Pivot_Guide (6) are reference layers and belong in neither.

face.note: measured from a rendered plate, not by hand. Width is the muzzle's full skin extent where the mouth sits - the dog's snout is broken up by its nose and stitching, so a largest-contiguous-run measure reads far too narrow.

eye_note: white eyeballs with black pupils, unlike the doctor's flat discs. Found as enclosed white regions - white connected to the border is background.

mouth_source.command: uv run rig.py mouths <rig> --element 34 --out /tmp/dogall --map D1=1,...,D20=20  then  uv run face.py derive /tmp/dogall --out assets/rigs/dog/mouths --spec ...
mouth_source.note: Of the dog's 20 drawings only 16, 1 and 11 are drawn head-on (symmetry 0.96-0.97). The rest lean, and cutting between leaning mouths makes it appear to swing side to side. Scaling a symmetric mouth keeps it symmetric, so the vowel set is derived from those three: OO is drawing 1 at 55% width (a pucker), EE the same drawing stretched wide and flat.

capability_note: Only 3 of the 20 drawings are head-on; the vowel set is derived from those by non-uniform scaling. The lips do not change shape, only the proportions of the opening - it moves convincingly but does not form words. Real drawn vowels would still be better. tears is false because the cheek routing has not been measured for this face.
